posts.title: iPhone Duo Review: A First-Generation Foldable, Eight Years Late
posts.description: I didn't buy this iPhone Duo. I borrowed one. Every other device I've reviewed here, I spent my actual money on. This one I didn't, and Apple didn't send it to me either. What it is The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable, on sale since 23 October. It opens like a book, with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner one. posts.title: The MNT Pocket Reform Is the Computer I Actually Own
posts.description: The MNT Pocket Reform is an okay system, if you're okay with its compromises. Every product is a package of emphasis, and the Pocket Reform is a more extreme package than most: MNT spent nearly everything on a few things they care about deeply and very little on several things most laptops treat as the baseline. posts.title: Be Aware of What's in Your Logs
posts.description: There is something I wish more people understood about bug reports, diagnostic information, and the apparently innocent act of attaching a log file to a support request, and it is this: your logs may contain things you really, really do not want anyone else reading. I'm writing this because of a bug report I received recently, which came with a log file containing information I did not need to see
